chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may Allah have mercy on him) told us of that, saying: Ahmad ibn Idris told us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, who said: Abu Muhammad Ja'far ibn Ahmad ibn Sa'id al-Bajali, the son of the brother of Safwan ibn Yahya, told us, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Saif ibn 'Umayra, from Abu al-Sabah ibn Na'im al-'A'idhi, from Muhammad ibn Muslim,

he said in a narration in which he says at its end: The Glorification of Fatima (peace be upon her) is among the abundant remembrance of Allah, about which Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, said: "And remember Me, I will remember you."

key_terms.تَسْبِيحُ فَاطِمَةَ: The Glorification of Fatima, a specific set of dhikr phrases attributed to Fatima al-Zahra
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Exalted and Glorious (a title for God)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Tasbih Fatima in Shia tradition and how does it relate to the Quran?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq, a pivotal figure in Twelver Shia scholarship, transmits this chain to validate 'Tasbih Fatima' as the quintessential form of abundant dhikr, linking it to the verse 'Wa idhkuruni adhkurkum'. This narration underscores the theological significance of this specific supplication as a direct fulfillment of the divine promise of reciprocal remembrance, a concept deeply cherished in Shia devotional practice.
